record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Given a graph G known to be the visibility graph of a finite point set P in the plane, construct coordinates for a point set whose visibility graph is G.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 Given the visibility graph G of a set of points, draw the points in the plane whose visibility graph is G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P = {p_1, ..., p_n} be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane in general position (no three collinear is not assumed; collinearity may block visibility). Two points p_i, p_j ∈ P are mutually visible if the open line segment connecting them contains no other point of P. The visibility graph of P is the simple undirected graph V(P) on vertex set {1, ..., n} in which {i, j} is an edge if and only if p_i and p_j are mutually visible.

Suppose a finite simple graph G is given together with the promise that there exists some finite point set P in the plane with V(P) ≅ G. Provide an algorithm (or constructive procedure) that, on input G, outputs explicit coordinates for a point set P' ⊂ ℝ² such that V(P') ≅ G.
artifact.status_search_result: The reconstruction problem for point visibility graphs remains open. Recognition of point visibility graphs is known to be complete for the existential theory of the reals (Cardinal–Hoffmann, 2015), and there exist point visibility graphs that admit no realization with rational/integer coordinates, indicating fundamental obstacles to constructive reconstruction. No general polynomial-time or constructive algorithm to produce coordinates from a given (promised) point visibility graph is known.

status_evidence.title: Recognition and Complexity of Point Visibility Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recognition of point visibility graphs is complete for the existential theory of the reals; some PVGs require irrational coordinates.
status_evidence.claim: Recognition is ∃ℝ-complete, and reconstruction faces coordinate-realizability obstructions, indicating the problem is still open in general.

status_evidence.title: Visibility Graph Theory for Points (Ghosh, lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: The visibility graph recognition and reconstruction problems are long-standing open problems; only partial results are known.
status_evidence.claim: Reconstruction of point visibility graphs is explicitly listed as an open problem.
